clinician.trajectory_summary: The patient presented with prodromal right-sided neck pain on day 1, followed by an erythematous vesicular rash on day 4 initially misdiagnosed as contact dermatitis. By day 9, the rash spread to involve the right anterior chest, neck, and shoulder in a C2-C4 dermatomal distribution with dull, achy, and intermittent sharp pain. On day 12, she developed right ear discomfort, difficulty hearing, and a similar rash along the auricle (with normal external auditory canal). On day 14, she presented with partial right-sided facial paralysis, completing the classic triad for Ramsay Hunt Syndrome (facial nerve palsy, auricular vesicles, and auditory symptoms). RHS was diagnosed clinically in the Emergency Room without laboratory confirmation. Treatment was initiated with valacyclovir (extended to 10 days), prednisone, and neuro-ophthalmology referral for eye protection. By day 46, she showed significant improvement with symmetric smile and complete right eye closure.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Prodromal right-sided neck pain preceding rash onset
Erythematous vesicular rash initially misdiagnosed as contact dermatitis on day 4
Progression to C2-C4 dermatomal distribution involving right anterior chest, neck, and shoulder by day 9
Auricular rash with ear discomfort and hearing difficulty on day 12
Partial right-sided facial paralysis on day 14 completing the classic RHS triad
Clinical diagnosis of RHS in Emergency Room with initiation of valacyclovir and prednisone
Neuro-ophthalmology referral made for eye protection due to facial palsy
Significant clinical improvement with resolution of facial paralysis by day 46

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Initial misdiagnosis on day 4; however, the dermatomal distribution, progression to auricular involvement, and development of facial paralysis are inconsistent with contact dermatitis
While facial paralysis was present, the presence of auricular vesicles and auditory symptoms (hearing difficulty) distinguishes RHS from isolated Bell's palsy
External auditory canal was normal on day 12 examination, and the vesicular rash along the auricle is inconsistent with bacterial otitis

remaining_uncertainties: No laboratory confirmation (VZV PCR, serology, or Tzanck smear) was documented to definitively confirm varicella zoster virus infection
Specific findings from the neuro-ophthalmology consultation were not documented
Detailed audiology findings or specific character of hearing difficulty (sensorineural vs conductive) were not specified
